newsitem.title: USA: American Air "disappointed" labor deal rejected.
newsitem.headline: American Air "disappointed" labor deal rejected.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said it was "extremely disappointed" that its pilots had rejected a proposed four-year labor contract but did not immediately comment on how the move might affect plans to overhaul its fleet.
American Airlines said in a statement it was "extremely disappointed that the members of the Allied Pilots Association (APA) failed to ratify the tentative agreement reached September 2, 1996".
It said it was consulting with the APA and the National Mediation Board about the future of the wage negotiations.
APA spokesman Gregg Overman said 5,046 members voted against ratifying the proposed contract, with 3,197 in favor of it.

The airline last November pledged to buy 103 jets from Boeing Co and take out options on 527 more in one of the biggest commerical aircraft orders ever. At the time, it said it would only proceed with an overhaul of its fleet if pilots approved the labor contract.
American Airlines did not address the issue of the Boeing aircraft deal in its statement, and company officials did not return telephone calls.

Under the tentative agreement, which was struck last September after two years of often bitter negotiations, pilots would have received a 3.0 percent pay raise in August 1997 and another 2.0 percent in August 1999.
The APA board of directors had approved the contract in November and recommended that members follow suit.
Overman said the union's board of directors would meet in Fort Worth on Thursday to discuss their next step.
American Airlines said the National Mediation Board could declare an impasse in the negotiations and offer binding arbitration to both sides.
The carrier said that if either party then rejected arbitration, a 30-day cooling-off period would begin.

"If there is no agreement by the conclusion of this period, the union would be free to strike, and the airline would be free to implement new pay and work rules it bargained over during the negotiations," American Airlines said.
